 MADISON (WKOW) — The Wisconsin Department of Transportation Division of Motor Vehicles will keep customer service centers open until 6 p.m. on Nov. 2 and Nov. 3 to give voters more time to get a photo ID.
Voters who don't have a Wisconsin driver license, ID or other form of identification needed to vote can still get a Wisconsin ID from the DMV. There is no separate "voter ID" and a federally compliant REAL ID card is not required for voting purposes.
The Wisconsin Elections Commission website explains the options for IDs to show at the polls.
To get an official Wisconsin ID card, voters need documentation such as a birth certificate, proof of identity and Wisconsin residency. Voters should bring any documentation available to the DMV and fill out two forms.
DMV's new Find My DMV locator helps customers find a convenient site. A photo ID document will be sent via overnight mail that may be taken to the polls and used for voting.
Completing a provisional ballot may be an option until the photo ID document arrives.
DMV offers ID cards for voting purposes to U.S. citizens free of charge. DMV's toll-free hotline at (844) 588-1069 is available for questions on obtaining an ID for voting purposes.
Questions regarding voter eligibility, poll locations, voter registration information or other election information may be found on the Wisconsin Elections Commission website elections.wi.gov.
